newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia cool on "crackpot historian" visit.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia cool on "crackpot historian" visit.

text.p: British historian David Irving, whose main claim to fame is his view that the Jewish Holocaust never happened, sparked an outcry on Wednesday with renewed plans to visit Australia, citing a new climate of free speech.
Politicians and community groups urged Prime Minister John Howard's government to refuse Irving a visa, warning he would provoke trouble and community division.

"There are certain circumstances in which words can become weapons and those words can cause harm and injury," prominent Jewish leader Mark Leibler told Australian Broadcasting Corporation (ABC) radio.

"I don't think that there is any principle of freedom of speech which requires a government, under these circumstances, to allow people such as Irving to come into this country and to spread their viscious villification," Liebler said.
Howard himself dismissed Irving as "a crackpot historian", but declined to pre-empt what the decision would be when Irving eventually applied for a visa.

Irving, condemned by critics as a Nazi apologist, said on Tuesday he would renew his previously refused application to visit Australia after Howard said his new conservative government had opened a fresh climate of free speech.
"In his (Howard's) view, there is now a new climate of freedom of speech now blowing in Australia," Irving told ABC radio from the United States.
Irving, barred from entry by the former Labor government in 1992, said he was confident that he would be allowed in by Howard's Liberal-National government.
Irving has been banned from Austria, Germany and Canada for his view that the Holocaust, in which about six million Jews were killed under Germany's Adolf Hitler, never happened.
The controversial historian said he would include a copy of Howard's weekend comments on freedom of speech in his visa application, to be lodged on his return to Britain next month.
Howard said in a weekend speech that his conservative government, elected in March, had lifted "a pall of censorship on certain issues" since winning office.

Asked about the outcry by Channel Nine television, Howard said on Wednesday: "Let me say I think David Irving is, to put it bluntly, a crackpot historian. Anybody who says the Holocaust didn't occur is a nutter."

"You're asking me whether if he applies again (for a visa) will we admit him, and the answer is that will be considered according to the criteria, and I'm not going to pre-empt what that decision will be. He hasn't even made the application yet.
"There was an element of opportunism and gimmickry in his jumping on the television yesterday, and I'm not going to play his game of opportunism and gimmickry," he said.
